notes: WholePath Pet free-planner rule library. Legal entry requirements are separated from recommendations and carrier/local rules.

Japan.authority: USDA APHIS / Japan Animal Quarantine Service

requirements.summary: ISO-compatible microchip; normally implanted on or before the first qualifying rabies vaccination.
At least two qualifying rabies vaccinations after microchipping; first at 91 days of age or older; second more than 30 days later while the first remains valid.
Rabies antibody test of at least 0.5 IU/mL from an accepted laboratory.
At least 180 days from the titer blood draw to arrival.
Advance notification to Animal Quarantine Service at least 40 days before arrival.
Final veterinary examination, export health certificate, and USDA APHIS endorsement for U.S. departures.
Microchip identification; the rabies vaccination used for entry cannot predate identification.
Valid rabies vaccination; a primary vaccination generally requires at least a 21-day wait before travel.
EU animal health certificate for non-commercial movement from the United States, with competent-authority endorsement.
Dogs entering Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway, or Northern Ireland require Echinococcus treatment 24–120 hours before entry.

Rabies documentation depends on species, age, origin, and travel circumstances; a current rabies vaccination certificate is the common pathway for ordinary U.S.-origin dogs and cats old enough to require it.
No universal federal microchip requirement for ordinary accompanied U.S.-origin pet dogs and cats.
Effective August 3, 2026, U.S.-origin pet dogs require an NWS Inspection Certificate signed by a USDA-accredited veterinarian and issued no more than 5 days before travel.
U.S.-origin pet cats do not currently require a health certificate for entry to Mexico.
SENASICA arrival inspection for signs of infectious disease, ectoparasites, and fresh or healing wounds.

South Africa.authority: USDA APHIS / Republic of South Africa

requirements.summary: Veterinary import permit required for dogs and cats.
U.S.-origin dogs must test negative for Trypanosoma evansi using both CATT and Giemsa blood-smear tests at accepted laboratories.
The dog microchip number must appear on laboratory reports.
Veterinary health certificate must be USDA APHIS endorsed; for U.S.-origin dogs issuance and endorsement must occur within 10 days of travel.

Hawaii.authority: Hawaii Department of Agriculture Animal Quarantine Station

requirements.summary: Microchip required to identify the pet for FAVN testing and faster-release pathways.
Two qualifying rabies vaccinations are required for the 5 Day Or Less / Direct Airport Release pathways.
Passing OIE-FAVN result of at least 0.5 IU/mL.
30-day pre-arrival wait after the laboratory receives the FAVN sample for the 5 Day Or Less pathway.

domestic.scope: Privately owned dogs and cats traveling with their owner, without sale, adoption, rescue transfer, or change of ownership.

defaults.cvi: Use the conservative state-entry plan: carry a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection issued within 30 days before entry. Owner-accompanied exemptions can be narrower than they appear and do not override airline rules.

rabies.dog: Carry a current rabies vaccination certificate. Dogs below the state vaccination age must still meet any age, confinement, or local rules.
rabies.cat: Carry a current rabies vaccination certificate even where state entry law does not expressly require it; local jurisdictions and carriers can require proof.

Alabama.authority: Alabama Department of Agriculture and Industries

domestic.cvi: A CVI issued within 30 days before entry is required for dogs and cats.

rabies.dog: Dogs 3 months or older must have a current rabies vaccination certificate.
rabies.cat: Carry a current rabies certificate; local and carrier rules may apply.

domestic.special: An import permit is required when the animal comes from an area quarantined for rabies.

domestic.cvi: A CVI issued within 30 days before entry is the standard entry document for dogs and cats.

rabies.dog: Dogs 3 months or older must have current rabies vaccination proof.

domestic.cvi: A CVI issued within 30 days before entry is the standard entry document.

rabies.dog: Dogs 4 months or older must have current rabies vaccination proof.
rabies.cat: Cats 4 months or older should travel with current rabies proof.

California.authority: California Department of Food and Agriculture

domestic.cvi: California does not require a CVI for a privately owned dog or cat accompanied by its owner when there is no sale, adoption, or ownership change.

rabies.dog: Dogs 4 months or older must be currently vaccinated against rabies; carry the certificate.
rabies.cat: California does not impose a statewide rabies entry requirement for cats, but local jurisdictions and carriers may require vaccination proof.

Florida.authority: Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services

domestic.cvi: A privately owned dog or cat traveling with its owner for personal travel is exempt from Florida’s Official Certificate of Veterinary Inspection requirement.
domestic.rabies: Dogs and cats 3 months or older must have current rabies vaccination proof.

domestic.cvi: A privately owned dog or cat accompanying its owner for leisure travel is exempt from Georgia’s CVI requirement.
domestic.rabies: Dogs and cats must be currently vaccinated against rabies; carry the certificate.

Hawaii.authority: Hawaii Department of Agriculture Animal Quarantine Station

domestic.cvi: Hawaii requires its Dog & Cat Import Form and an original health certificate in the applicable arrival window; the exact checklist depends on Direct Airport Release, 5 Day Or Less, or quarantine pathway.
domestic.rabies: For Direct Airport Release or 5 Day Or Less, the pet needs two qualifying rabies vaccinations and a passing OIE-FAVN test tied to its microchip.
domestic.special: Microchip identification, a passing OIE-FAVN result, the required waiting period, advance document submission, fees, and an approved arrival airport are central to faster release. Missing a step can result in quarantine.

domestic.cvi: A CVI issued within 30 days before entry is required and must include a physical description that identifies the animal.
domestic.rabies: Carry a current rabies vaccination certificate.

Iowa.authority: Iowa Department of Agriculture and Land Stewardship

Louisiana.authority: Louisiana Department of Agriculture and Forestry

Maine.authority: Maine Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry

domestic.cvi: Dogs and cats entering Massachusetts need a health certificate that identifies the animal and addresses health and rabies exposure.
domestic.rabies: For animals older than 6 months, the certificate must document rabies vaccination within the required period. An unvaccinated younger animal must be vaccinated within 30 days after entry or at 6 months of age, whichever is later.

Michigan.authority: Michigan Department of Agriculture and Rural Development

domestic.cvi: A CVI is required unless a listed exemption applies. Minnesota accepts electronic CVIs for covered imports; confirm the veterinarian submits the accepted form.

New Hampshire.authority: New Hampshire Department of Agriculture, Markets & Food

New York.authority: New York State Department of Agriculture and Markets

North Carolina.authority: North Carolina Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services

Oklahoma.authority: Oklahoma Department of Agriculture, Food and Forestry

domestic.cvi: Dogs and cats entering Oregon need a CVI issued within 30 days before entry. For a short round trip, ask the veterinarian whether the original outbound CVI can cover the return within its validity window.

Rhode Island.authority: Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management

Texas.authority: Texas Department of State Health Services

domestic.cvi: Texas does not require a CVI for ordinary interstate entry of a privately owned dog or cat.

rabies.dog: Dogs 12 weeks or older must have a current rabies vaccination certificate. A dog younger than 12 weeks must be confined until 30 days after its initial vaccination.
rabies.cat: Cats 12 weeks or older must have a current rabies vaccination certificate. A younger cat must meet the applicable confinement and vaccination rule.

Utah.authority: Utah Department of Agriculture and Food

Vermont.authority: Vermont Agency of Agriculture, Food and Markets

Virginia.authority: Virginia Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services

domestic.cvi: A dog or cat accompanying its owner is exempt from a CVI when the owner has had the animal for more than one month and there is no ownership change. Emergency disease-zone rules can override this exemption.
domestic.rabies: Dogs and cats must have current rabies vaccination proof.
domestic.special: Animals arriving from a federally designated New World screwworm affected area are subject to Washington’s emergency entry conditions, including a recent CVI and parasite inspection documentation. If the trip originates outside such an area, this emergency condition does not apply.

Wisconsin.authority: Wisconsin Department of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection
